source_text:
Ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς οἰκονομίας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Λόγου τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ εὐδοκίᾳ τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ
συνεργίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος σαρκωθέντος, δύο φύσεις ὁμολογοῦμεν, καὶ μίαν
ὑπόστασιν· ἕνα τε Υἱὸν τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν, Θεὸν ὁμοῦ καὶ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ
ἓν πρόσωπον· δύο δὲ θελήσεις καὶ δύο ἐνεργείας· ἑκάστην φύσιν μετὰ τῆς ἰδιότητος,
ἀδιαιρέτως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως.
orientation: John of Damascus turns from the Trinity to the economy of the incarnate Word, confessing two natures in one person.
pass_a_gloss: But in the case of the economy of God and Word of God, that is, the Incarnation, the [one] having been made flesh by the good pleasure of the Father and by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, two natures we confess, and one person; and one Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, God together and man, and one person; but two wills and two activities; each nature with the property, without division and without confusion.

choices.english: But in the case of the economy
choices.why: ἐπί with genitive marks the sphere or domain under discussion; the δέ signals a transition from the theology of the Trinity to the economy.

choices.english: the one having been made flesh by the good pleasure of the Father
choices.why: The participle σαρκωθέντος is attributive to Λόγου; εὐδοκίᾳ is a dative of means or attendant circumstance, rendered with 'by' to show agency of the Father's will.
rejected: who was incarnate by the Father's will
having become flesh through the Father's approval

choices.term: δύο φύσεις ὁμολογοῦμεν, καὶ μίαν ὑπόστασιν
choices.english: two natures we confess, and one person
choices.why: The verb ὁμολογοῦμεν governs both accusatives; the word order is kept in the literal gloss to preserve the confessional formula's emphasis.
rejected: we confess two natures and one hypostasis
we acknowledge two natures and one person

choices.why: ὁμοῦ means 'together' or 'at the same time,' stressing the simultaneity of divinity and humanity in the one Christ.

The accusative ἑκάστην φύσιν is the object of an implied verb of having or keeping; μετά with genitive means 'with' in the sense of accompaniment, preserving the idea that each nature retains its own property.
rejected: each nature along with its property
every nature with its distinctive property

pass_b_english: But in the economy of God and the Word of God, who was made flesh by the good pleasure of the Father and the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, we confess two natures and one person: one Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, God together with man, and one person. We confess also two wills and two activities, each nature keeping its property, without division and without confusion.

problems.quote: we confess two natures and one person
problems.why: Unclear if authorial voice or creedal quotation.
problems.fix: Clarify this is the author's confession of faith.

problems.why: Ambiguous: could mean 'God alongside man' not 'God-man'; risks Nestorian misreading.
problems.fix: Render as 'both God and man' or 'the God-man'.

problems.quote: economy of God and the Word of God
problems.why: Same event named differently; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Add 'that is, the Incarnation' after first occurrence.

variants.text: economy of God and the Word of God

edits.old: we confess two natures and one person
edits.new: we ourselves confess two natures and one person

fixed: The English 'we confess two natures and one person' already reflects the author's confession; the source has no explicit quotation, so no change was needed beyond clarifying the authorial voice.
The English 'God together with man' was ambiguous and could suggest a Nestorian reading; changed to 'both God and man' to match the source's 'Θεὸν ὁμοῦ καὶ ἄνθρωπον'.
The glossary issue about 'economy of God and the Word of God' was addressed by adding 'that is, the Incarnation' to the literal gloss, not the English, since the English already reads naturally.
